sources.read_scope: Section2, Lemma1, Fact1; section2.1 basic and extended modular strategies through Assumption1, pp3-5
sources.notes: The modular construction normalizes an invertible leading coefficient and selects monomial shifts from nested support sets. Its integer lattice has scaled coefficient rows vanishing modulo a power of the modulus. The norm bound and integer-root conclusion are separate from the heuristic final multivariate recovery assumption. Extended strategies add designated variable shifts; the exact choice must be frozen for the ECC experiment.

sources.notes: The paper relates Frobenius action to scalar action on the chosen unique prime-order subgroup. Orbit-based factor-base construction reduces unknowns under stated hypotheses. Sparse linear algebra is costed using row weight and matrix size. The abstract reductions alone do not certify an observed displacement-rank solver or a universal ECDLP lower bound.
